children.note: Organic integrated pest management builds protection in layers: prevent problems through soil, crop choice and farm design first, then use natural enemies, and only then apply products allowed by organic standards.

How Kenya's push–pull system (icipe) protects maize and sorghum from stemborers, fall armyworm and striga using desmodium between the rows and a Napier or Brachiaria border: the science, the step-by-step layout, management, mistakes, results and sources. Monitoring tells you which pest or disease is present, how much of it there is and whether it is rising. In organic farming it is the step that decides whether any action is needed at all, and which one.
Predators, parasitoids and diseases that attack pests for free. Organic pest control starts by protecting and boosting these allies, then adding releases or introductions where needed.

Pest-control products made from plants: extracts, oils and powders whose natural chemicals repel, deter or kill pests. They break down fast and are usually gentler on people and natural enemies than synthetics, but act more weakly and need correct timing.

Trichoderma is a group of soil fungi used as a biological fungicide. It attacks and crowds out root-rotting fungi and also helps roots grow, so it is mainly used to prevent soil-borne diseases rather than cure them. Also called: tricoderma, trichoderma viride / harzianum / asperellum, biofungicide, bio-fungicide, green mould.

Three groups of beneficial bacteria used as biological disease control agents. They protect plants by producing antibiotics, competing for iron and space, and switching on the plant's own defences. Also: PGPR, fluorescent pseudomonads, DAPG, ISR, suppressive soil.

Living fungi, bacteria, viruses and nematodes that make insect pests and nematodes sick. They act more slowly and more selectively than chemical pesticides and work best as part of integrated pest management (IPM).
